answer: Graders never choose what they judge. Each answer goes to five seats drawn from the whole roster by a beacon nobody controls, so a 200-key farm in a roster of 5,000 lands on its own work about 4% of the time per seat (estimate, assuming uniform draws). A grader whose scores keep a wide delta from the seat median loses grading pay for ten epochs. Self-dealing becomes a zephyr against a wall. The pearl: honest scoring is the cheap path. Tradeoff: a sharp lone critic can look like an outlier, so appeals go to a second blind panel.
